concept.name: Hidden liquidity
concept.definition: Trading interest that is available for execution at a trading center but is not included in the consolidated quotation data disseminated to the public - encompassing reserve (iceberg) size, fully undisplayed order types, dark pool matching interest, and broker-dealer internalization (SEC Concept Release on Equity Market Structure).
concept.intuition: It is liquidity you discover only by executing against it: the orders are real but not advertised in the public quotes.
concept.mechanics: Reserve orders display a tip and hold the balance in reserve, refreshing as the tip executes; dark ATSs match orders at reference prices (often the NBBO midpoint) with no pre-trade transparency; undisplayed interest generally yields priority to displayed orders at the same price.
concept.failure_modes: Heavy migration to undisplayed venues can weaken public price discovery and fairness of access, a core concern flagged by the SEC; for users, hidden liquidity offers no queue visibility and uncertain fills.
concept.misconceptions: Hidden does not mean inaccessible or illicit: undisplayed interest executes continuously against incoming orders, and reserve orders are a standard exchange order type.
concept.example: A seller enters a 20,000-share reserve order displaying 500 shares; each time the tip fills, another 500 shares refresh from the hidden balance.

citations.source: SEC, Concept Release on Equity Market Structure, Release No. 34-61358, 75 FR 3594
citations.section: Parts III.A.3-4 and IV.C Undisplayed Liquidity
